reference.title: across or through
reference.text: across = from one side to the other of something with ‘sides’ (a square, a street, a river): He swam across the river. through = from one side to the other ‘in something’ (a forest, a tunnel, a crowd): We walked through the crowds.

reference.title: away and back
reference.text: away = to another place: Go away! I don’t want to speak to you. The man ran away when he saw the policeman. back = to the place where somebody or something was before: After dinner we went back to our hotel.

reference.title: Sports verbs
reference.text: hit the ball over the net (tennis), kick the ball into the goal (football), throw the ball through the hoop (basketball), run round the track (athletics).

reference.why: play only with ball sports; do karate, yoga, gymnastics, athletics.
go + verb + -ing for sports like skiing, cycling, windsurfing.

reference.title: Verb of movement + preposition / adverb
rows: The ball went over the goalkeeper’s head and into the goal.
He drove out of the car park and along the street.
I ran over the bridge and across the park.

reference.text: To express movement, use a verb of movement (go, come, run, walk, drive, cycle…) + a preposition or adverb (up, down, over, across, away…).

reference.title: come or go?
reference.text: come = movement towards you (Come here, please!); go = movement away from you (Go away. You’re so annoying!).

reference.title: in or into? out or out of?
reference.text: into / out of + a noun: Come into the living room. He went out of the house. in / out without a noun: Come in. He went out.

reference.right: He went out of the house.

reference.why: No noun after it – use in, not into.

reference.title: Talking about sport
reference.text: Do you do any sport? – Yes, I play football / go running / do yoga. I’m a fan of… I’ve been to… (a live match). The most exciting sporting event I’ve ever watched was…

reference.title: An article: Why I love…
reference.text: Paragraph 1 – basic information about the activity. Paragraph 2 – when and why you started. Paragraph 3 – why you enjoy it. Paragraph 4 – recommend it to the reader (you should try it!).

tasks.instruction: Sport – you love it or you hate it. Talk to a partner
tasks.note: SB 2 Speaking (+ Writing 5a «Do you see people doing sport or exercise in your town?») → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You talk about sport: ‘Sport – you love it or you hate it’. Ask these questions one at a time and ask for more information: Do you do any sport or exercise? (Yes – What? Do you enjoy it? / No – Why not? Did you do more sport or exercise in the past? Why do you do less now?) Which sports do you think are the most exciting to watch? Which are the most boring? Are you (or is anyone in your family) a fan of a sports team? Which one? Do you (or they) go to their matches? Have you ever been to any live sporting events? What is the most exciting sporting event you have ever been to or watched on TV? Do you see people doing sport or exercise in your town? What do you see them doing? When the student asks you, answer too: you go running and do yoga, you think tennis is exciting and golf is boring, you once went to a Champions League final. If the student says play karate or go to ski, repeat the correct phrase (do karate, go skiing) naturally.
exercises.goal: Talk about sport you do and watch.
exercises.opener: Hi! Let’s talk about sport. Do you do any sport or exercise?
criteria: answers at least four questions with extra information
uses play / go / do + sport correctly
uses the present perfect for experiences (I’ve been to…, I’ve never…)
asks the partner at least one question back

steps.text: Say what sport or exercise you do
steps.example: I go swimming twice a week and I sometimes do yoga.

steps.text: Say which sports are exciting or boring to watch
steps.example: I think football is the most exciting, and golf is really boring.

steps.text: Talk about a team you or your family support
steps.example: My dad is a big fan of Spartak, but he doesn’t go to their matches.

steps.text: Describe the most exciting sporting event you have seen
steps.example: The most exciting event I’ve ever watched was the World Cup final.

steps.text: Say what sport people do in your town
steps.example: In my town, a lot of people go cycling or running in the park.

tasks.instruction: Read the comments on a forum. Find one person who obviously prefers women’s sport and one who obviously prefers men’s sport
tasks.note: SB 4b → Blank на имя или букву комментария. Ответы MODEL (женский спорт — A RichSmith, также можно F ZoeCruz)
tasks.context:
Why aren’t women’s sports as popular as men’s? Send us your thoughts.

A RichSmith: I actually prefer watching women’s tennis. Men usually hit the ball so hard, especially when they serve, that their opponent can’t return it, so it’s less exciting to watch.

B WayneKeys: I think we should open up men’s football to women. Then we could compare, person to person, how well each player performs, and teams could be made up of the best players, both men and women. That’s true of most team sports, actually.

C Brandi: Women’s sports that are identical to men’s sports – football and basketball, for example – will never be as popular as men’s, because men are faster, stronger and more athletic. On the other hand, sports that highlight the strengths of female athletes – tennis, gymnastics, ice skating – are popular. But it’s interesting that none of those are team sports.

D Lynn228: Brandi, I think you’re right about the difference between team and individual sports. When I watch the Olympics (winter and summer), I enjoy the women’s and men’s individual events equally. The women probably run / swim / ski a bit slower than the men, but I can’t really tell, and it’s just as exciting.

E SimonB: Most people want to watch the best sports people perform at the highest level. If you compare top male and female athletes, physical differences mean that women are always inferior athletes to men.

F ZoeCruz: In men’s football, the players fall over all the time and act like babies. The women don’t do that. I’ve read research that says that women hardly ever pretend to be hurt. And when they are hurt, they get up again 30 seconds faster than men.

exercises.explain: RichSmith: ‘I actually prefer watching women’s tennis.’ (ZoeCruz also clearly likes women’s football more.)
SimonB: ‘women are always inferior athletes to men.’

tasks.instruction: Talk about women’s sport. Which comments do you agree with? Why?
tasks.note: SB 4a (вопросы для обсуждения) + 4e (Tick the comments you agree with… compare with a partner) → разговор с ИИ

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You have both read six forum comments about the question ‘Why aren’t women’s sports as popular as men’s?’: A women’s tennis is more exciting because men hit the ball too hard; B men and women should play football together in the same teams; C women’s team sports will never be as popular as men’s, but individual sports like tennis, gymnastics and ice skating are; D women’s and men’s individual events at the Olympics are equally exciting; E men are always better athletes; F women footballers don’t pretend to be hurt like men. First ask: Do you ever watch women’s sport? Are they team sports or individual sports? In your country, are there any women’s sports that are as popular as men’s? Then ask which comments the student agrees with and why, and what they think about the others. Give your own opinion too: you agree with D and F, and you don’t agree with E. Keep your answers short and friendly.
exercises.goal: Say which comments you agree with and why.
exercises.opener: Do you ever watch women’s sport? What do you watch?
criteria: answers the questions about women’s sport in their country
says which comments they agree or disagree with (I agree with… because…)

tasks.instruction: Read the article again. Which paragraph…? Write the number
tasks.note: Writing 7 a+c; «Why does the writer enjoy parkrun?» → пункт 1; порядок абзацев → Blank с номером. MODEL
tasks.context:
Why I love parkrun by Rachel Farrah

1 Parkrun organizes free five kilometre runs all over the world. Every Saturday morning, in the UK and in lots of other countries, people meet in a park and go for a run together. After the run you get a text message which tells you your time, so you can see that you’re getting faster and fitter.

2 I started doing parkrun three years ago. I was overweight and stressed, and a friend invited me to go to the local run with him, in Princes Park here in Liverpool. I really didn’t want to go at first, but after a few weeks I felt much better. Now I try to do it every Saturday, and I’ve done more than 100 runs since I started.

3 I love parkrun because of the people who do it – the atmosphere is really friendly, and it’s much more fun and motivating to run with other people. I know that my running friends will be in the park at the same time every weekend, and that makes me get up and get out of the house.

4 It doesn’t matter if you’re old or young, male or female, fast or slow – if you want a healthy start to the weekend, you should try it! And if there isn’t a parkrun in your town or city, maybe you should start one!
